description: Painted sprite parts for the rebel queen, the scrapper with the frying pan (?art=paint). Same three steps as paint-rebel-pawn.json; then tools/art/cut-parts.mjs.

steps.name: pose
steps.prompt: Full-body game sprite of the rebel QUEEN from the first image, painted in the art style of the second image (a character select sheet). Use the third image only for the full-body pose and chunky proportions, not for its style. SUBJECT: a tough scrappy rebel queen. A dented grey steel kettle helm with a wide brim that droops at both ends, rust patches and one dent, and a small squat gold crown with three points and a red gem welded on top of it, a little crooked. Under the brim a small stern skin face with two black dot eyes, short angry brows and a flat frowning mouth. A rusty grey steel breastplate on straps over a cream apron with a frayed hem, a mauve-brown shirt with short patched sleeves, a bright purple armband tied on her left upper arm, grey gauntlets, short dark boots. A big black cast-iron frying pan held upright in her right fist on the right side of the figure: her fist is clearly wrapped round the pan's straight handle, the fingers visibly gripping it, with the round pan raised beside her helm and turned a little so its face is a tilted oval with a lighter grey rim. The pan is narrow from the side: no wider than her helm's brim. Standing, three-quarter view facing right, feet visible, chunky and big-headed: the helm and crown are about half the figure's height. STYLE to match the second image exactly: bold flash-era 2D brawler cartoon, very thick even black outlines, flat fills, one hard cel shadow, crisp white highlights on metal, earthy rusty colours with the purple armband as the one bright accent. One character only, centred, on a plain flat light grey background (#d8d8d8), no ground, no cast shadow, no text, no labels, no frame.

steps.name: parts
steps.prompt:
Cut this exact character into separate parts for a 2D cut-out puppet, like a paper-doll sprite sheet. Keep her exact art style, colours, outline thickness and shading. Draw each part whole and complete, including the bits that are normally hidden behind other parts, and give every part its own very thick black outline all the way round. The parts are separate stickers with wide empty gaps between them, every part at the same scale as in the first image, on a plain flat light grey background (#d8d8d8). The image holds only these parts and nothing else: no other characters, no tiles, no text, no labels, no numbers, no grid lines, no cast shadows.

Layout, exactly:
- Top row, left: the HEAD: the dented steel kettle helm with the small gold crown welded on top. The face under the brim is plain blank skin with NO eyes and NO eyebrows, only the small flat frowning mouth. The head ends at the chin, no neck.
- Top row, middle: the BODY: the rusty breastplate on straps over the cream apron with the frayed hem, the mauve-brown shirt, the legs and dark boots, with no arms and no head; a short skin neck stump at the top.
- Top row, right: the BACK ARM (her left arm): a short patched mauve sleeve with the bright purple armband tied round it, hanging down to a grey gauntlet fist.
- Bottom row, left: the FRONT ARM (her right arm): a short patched mauve sleeve from the shoulder, bent at the elbow, ending in a closed grey gauntlet fist that points to the right, curled as if round a handle.
- Bottom row, middle: empty.
- Right edge, spanning from top to bottom: the FRYING PAN on its own, standing upright with the pan at the top and the straight handle pointing down, the pan a tilted oval, whole and not held.
